xl/worksheets/sheet6.xml: A1: How to read

A2: Wheel pair numbers | B2: Counted on the side facing the camera, 1 = rearmost wheel (tender end), increasing towards the front. A wheel pair = one axle. Partly hidden wheels are counted and marked 'half hidden'; wheels that cannot be seen at all are not counted.

A3: Wheel labels | B3: driver = coupled driving wheel (rods); leading / trailing = small carrying wheels ahead of / behind the drivers; pony = single-axle truck; guide = GG1 guiding truck; bogie = wheel in a diesel/electric bogie; tender = tender wheel.
A4: Visible wheel pairs | B4: Formula: COUNTA over the 16 wheel cells of the row.

A5: Class (Size) | B5: Formula from 'Size (tiles)' via the Size classes sheet: 0.5 Skiff (XXS), 1 Corvette (XS), 2 Frigate (S), 3 Destroyer (M), 4 Cruiser (L), 5 Battleship (XL), 6 Juggernaut (XXL). The size is the image folder.

A6: Proposal logic | B6: Model-railway logic, following the game's docs/bogie-model.md: coupled steam drivers are rigid in the frame and drawn with the body; leading/trailing trucks and diesel/electric bogies swivel as separate sprites; size 0.5-1 stock keeps its axles baked into the body on 2 virtual supports. Prototype facts are only used to flag where the art differs.
A7: Narrow-gauge rows | B7: Pictures are the model images (front and rear view). Narrow-gauge track is not in the game yet. Reference photos stay in the loco folders; prototype data is web research.
